title: Serper vs Tavily
subtitle: AI Search API comparison · 2026
summary: Two AI search APIs, one decision. Serper sells cheap Google SERP JSON; Tavily sells LLM-ready page content and synthesis. Here is the evidence from the Lab 10 research run, side by side.

cards.title: Buy the SERP, skip the extraction.
cards.lede: The cheapest way to get Google's results page back as structured JSON.
points: Organic results, knowledge graph, People Also Ask, related searches
News, Maps, Shopping and Scholar verticals
Country and language targeting built in

cards.title: Buy the reading, not just the links.
cards.lede: Returns page content and a synthesized answer an agent can use immediately.
points: Snippet chunks plus raw page content in one request

chart.caption: Fig. 1 — Cost per 1,000 searches. Bars are drawn from the backend dataset.

items.title: You want Google results as JSON for far less
items.body: Serper runs $0.30–$1.00 per 1,000 searches against Tavily's $8.00 pay-as-you-go.

items.title: You need SERP features
items.body: Knowledge graph, People Also Ask, related searches and organic results come back structured.

items.title: You need other Google verticals
items.body: News, Maps, Shopping and Scholar, with country and language targeting built in.

items.title: You already fetch and parse pages
items.body: If you only need snippets, or you run your own scraper, Serper's SERP-only output is enough.

items.title: An LLM or RAG pipeline reads the results
items.body: Page content and an answer arrive in the same request, so the agent can act immediately.

items.title: You want RAG helpers
items.body: Answer synthesis and follow-up questions are built in, not bolted on.

items.title: You use LlamaIndex
items.body: Tavily has the mature LlamaIndex and LangChain integrations for agent grounding.

items.title: Your volume is small and steady
items.body: 1,000 free credits a month covers light research workloads with no card required.

warnings.title: Serper's weak spot
warnings.body: Page content lives on a separate Webpage endpoint with no public price, and credits expire after six months.

warnings.title: Tavily's weak spot
warnings.body: Costs 5–26.7× more per basic search, and advanced depth doubles the price.

sections.heading: The decision, in three questions
sections.body: Start from what the agent needs to do with the result, not from the price list. If the agent needs page content and an answer, choose Tavily. If it needs Google SERP features or the lowest cost, choose Serper. If neither applies, both work with LangChain — pick by budget and integration fit.
